cards.text: Jehoiada the priest has died at 130 and been buried with the kings (2 Chronicles 24:15-16). Now the officials of Judah come and pay homage to Joash, king of Judah. Friend, the only thing that ever bowed to me in the junk drawer I spent years in was an expired coupon somebody folded in half.

cards.question: With Jehoiada gone, the officials of Judah are bowing to King Joash. What does Joash do?

answers.text: He calls the priests in first

cards.question: Once King Joash starts listening to Judah's officials, they stay faithful to the house of the LORD.

cards.text: They abandon the house of the LORD, the God of their fathers, and serve Asherah poles and idols. Friend, that's walking out of a WARM bakery to go hug a cold fencepost.

cards.question: For this guilt of theirs, ___ comes upon Judah and Jerusalem.

cards.text: But the LORD doesn't give up on them. He sends prophets to bring the people back to Him and to testify against them.

cards.question: The LORD sends prophets to bring His people back to Him, but the people would not ___.

cards.text: You know when your phone keeps buzzing and you just flip it face down? That's Judah with the prophets God sends.
Then the Spirit of God comes upon Zechariah, son of Jehoiada the priest. He stands up before the people and tells them, "This is what God says…"

cards.question: Through Zechariah, God asks the people why they break the LORD's commandments. What does He say breaking them keeps them from?
Through Zechariah, God says that because the people have left the LORD, the LORD has left them.

cards.text: Friend, this is where the story turns cold. They conspire against Zechariah, and they stone him in the courtyard of the house of the LORD.

cards.question: Zechariah's attackers stone him on their own, with no order from King Joash.
When King Joash has Zechariah killed, he fails to remember the ___ that Zechariah's father Jehoiada had shown him.

cards.text: Instead, Joash kills Jehoiada's son. And as Zechariah lies dying, he speaks.

cards.question: What does Zechariah say as he lies dying?

answers.text: May the LORD see this and call you to account
May the LORD forgive you for what you have done
May the LORD remember my father's house

cards.text: In the spring, the army of Aram, a kingdom to the north, goes to war against Joash. They march right into Judah and Jerusalem.

cards.question: When the army of Aram enters Judah and Jerusalem, they destroy all the leaders of the people.

cards.text: They send all the plunder home to their king in Damascus, and Aram pulls all that off with only a FEW men. Friend, that's three people showing up to a tug-of-war and dragging the WHOLE other team across the line.

cards.question: Judah has a very great army. How do a few Aramean men beat it?

answers.text: The LORD hands Judah's army to them
Judah's soldiers switch to their side
They strike while Judah's army sleeps

cards.question: Because Judah had forsaken the LORD, the God of their fathers, judgment was executed on ___.

cards.text: When the Arameans pull out, they leave King Joash severely wounded.

cards.question: King Joash is lying severely wounded, and his own ___ conspire against him.
Why do Joash's servants conspire against him?

answers.text: For shedding the blood of Jehoiada's son
For losing the war against Aram
For taxing the people to repair the temple

cards.text: They kill Joash on his bed, and he is buried in the City of David. Not an enemy army, friend, but his OWN servants.

cards.question: Joash is buried in the tombs of the kings, just like Jehoiada the priest.

cards.text: The text names the two men who conspired against him: Zabad, son of Shimeath the Ammonitess, and Jehozabad, son of Shimrith the Moabitess.
More about Joash, his sons and the many pronouncements about him is written in the Treatise of the Book of the Kings. And his son Amaziah reigns in his place, friend.
